Diversity-Oriented Synthesis of Indole-Fused Polycyclic Scaffolds via
Rhodium-Catalyzed NH-Indole-Directed C−H Coupling of
2‑Phenyl‑1H‑indoles with Propargylic Alcohol Derivatives
Guijiao Xiang,
†
Yanqiao Wang,
†
Leipeng Lu, Xiaofeng Zhang, and Qiufeng Huang*

ABSTRACT: Diversity-oriented synthesis strategy for the efficient assembly of indole-fused polycyclic scaffolds via rhodium-
catalyzed NH-indole-directed C−H coupling with propargylic alcohol derivatives in a regioselective manner was developed. Five 2-
phenyl-1H-indole-embedded core skeletons were synthesized. In particular, three different indole-fused exo-olefin-containing
polycycles were realized, which may be manipulated for further chemistry.
■
INTRODUCTION
Indole-fused polycyclic scaffolds have been found in many
natural or unnatural compounds, showing a broad range of
structural diversities and biological activities.
1
In recent years,
diversity-oriented synthesis (DOS) has been an efficient
method for building libraries of small molecules with both
functional groups and skeletal diversity.
2
Consequently, the
development of new diversity-oriented synthesis for the
collections of indole-fused polycyclic molecules has gained
significant interest among synthetic chemists.
3
On the other
hand, metal-catalyzed C−H activations have emerged as a
powerful tool to synthesize functionalized complex molecules
in a sustainable manner.
4
Recently, our group
5
and others
6
have successfully developed the strategy of NH-indole-directed
C−H activation/annulation for the assembly of indole-fused
polycyclic structures via the reaction of 2-phenyl-1H-indoles or
7-phenyl-1H-indoles with various coupling partners. Unfortu-
nately, the coupling partners reported are limited to simple
monofunctional reagents, such as carbon monoxide,
5b
alkenes,
5aceh6g
alkynes,
5g6abf
or diazo compounds,
5df6h
which
inevitably lead to the poor structural diversity of target
products.
Propargylic alcohol derivatives are easily accessible from
terminal alkynes and ketones or aldehydes.
7
The presence of
the alkyne moiety and the OR unit in propargylic alcohol
derivatives endows diversified reactivity and an ideal synthetic
precursor for diversity-oriented synthesis.
8
As shown in
Scheme 1, metal-catalyzed directing group-assisted C−H
coupling with propargylic alcohol derivatives includes the
following common process. (1) Metal species A cleaves the
ortho-C−H bond of the substrate to generate metallacycle B.
9
(2) Migratory insertion of propargylic alcohol derivative into B
affords another metallacycle C. The weak coordination of an
oxygen atom with a metal catalyst would greatly benefit for
excellent region and chemoselectivity.
10
(3) C would undergo
the reductive elimination to release the annulated product D.
11
(4) β-Hydroxyl elimination of intermediate C would also
happen to produce allene F,
10c12
which can further undergo
intramolecular annulation to obtain various cyclic compounds
due to allene’s multiple reactive sites.
13
In this context,
propargylic alcohol derivatives have attracted considerable
attention recently for building a variety of cyclic molecules.
14
Bearing these in mind and as a continuation of our interest in

RESULTS AND DISCUSSION
Initially, we attempted the coupling reaction of the model
substrates 2-phenyl-1H-indole-3-carbaldehyde 1a and tert-
butyl (2-methyl-4-phenylbut-3-yn-2-yl) carbonate 2a. Encour-
agingly, we found that [Cp*RhCl
2
]
2
was capable of catalyzing
the reaction to produce the mixture of ortho-allenylated-2-
phenyl-1H-indole 3a and 5-phenyl-6-(prop-1-en-2-yl)indolo-
[2,1-a]isoquinoline-12-carbaldehyde 7a in yields of 31 and 8%,
respectively, using toluene as the solvent (Table 1, entry 1).
Further screening of other solvents indicated that EtOAc is the
most efficient solvent for selective allenylation to afford 3a in
71% yield (entries 2−6). The studies on the influence of
temperature showed that high temperature favored the
formation of 7a (entries 7−11). Performing the reaction at
100 °C resulted in a 42% yield of 7a (entry 10). However,
further increasing the temperature to 120 °C led to a messy
reaction mixture and provided only a trace of 3a or 7a (entry
11). Similar results were observed when the reaction was
carried out between 1a and 2-methyl-4-phenylbut-3-yn-2-yl
acetate (2b). The product 3a was isolated with 68% yield
(entry 12). For 2-methyl-4-phenylbut-3-yn-2-ol (2c), the
allenylated product 3 was not observed at all. Instead, the [4
+ 2] oxidative annulation product 6 was obtained in 20% yield
exclusively (entry 14). Many attempts to improve the yield of 6
were unsuccessful. Interestingly, the yield of 6 significantly
increased to 80% when the formyl group was removed from
substrate 1 (entry 15). Finally, subsequent acid-mediated
dehydration of 6 provided access to 7 in excellent yield (83%).
Control experiments showed that N-methyl substituted 2-
phenyl-1H-indole was unreactive in the process (entry 16).
The generality of 2-phenyl-1H-indoles for the allenylation
was first investigated, and the results are shown in Scheme 3.
The allenylation can be scaled up to the 5 mmol scale with the
optimal reaction conditions, and 3a was isolated in 56% yield
(1.1 g). The 2-phenyl-1H-indoles bearing groups at the meta-
and para-positions of the benzene ring underwent the
allenylation smoothly to give the corresponding products
3b−3i in good yields. In contrast, ortho-substituted substrate 1
afforded products 3j−3l in relatively low yields due to the
increased steric hindrance. For 2-phenyl-1H-indole, no

Next, the efficient construction of versatile indole-fused exo-
olefin-containing polycyclic compounds was realized by taking
advantage of the inherent multiple reactivities of the allenyl
motif (Scheme 4).

When ortho-allenylated-2-phenyl-1H-
indole 3a was treated with EtONa in N,N-dimethylformamide
(DMF) at 60 °C for 5 h, we observed exclusively 6-endo-dig
cyclization to give 5-phenyl-6-(propan-2-ylidene)-5,6-
dihydroindolo[2,1-a]isoquinoline 4a in excellent yield, whose
structure was confirmed by X-ray crystal diffraction. The
exploration of substrate scope, as shown in the left column of
Scheme 4, revealed that the base-mediated 6-endo-dig
hydroamination exhibited brilliant compatibility with various
substituents of 3. The yield of the corresponding product was
up to 97% (4a−4o). The 6-endo-dig cyclization of 3r delivered
a mixture of products 4p + 4p′ in total 82% yield. When the
cyclization of 3a was performed in the presence of the
Pd(OAc)
2
catalyst in cyclohexane at 100 °C, a 5-exo-trig
annulation product 5a instead of a 6-endo-dig product was
isolated. The structure of the 5-exo-trig annulation product was
unambiguously established by single-crystal X-ray analysis of
compound 5i. Ortho-allenylated-2-phenyl-1H-indoles featuring
different substituents proceeded to give the desired products
5a−5f and 5k−5l in moderate to good yields. Whereas the
yields were reduced to roughly 40% when the Cl or Br group
was present in the starting material 3 (5g−5j). Not
surprisingly, the 5-exo-trig annulation of 3r afforded a mixture
of products 5m + 5m′ (34% yield).
At the end, the oxidative annulation/dehydration cascade
reaction of 2-phenyl-1H-indoles with 2-methyl-4-phenylbut-3-
yn-2-ol was examined (Scheme 5). In most cases, 2-(5-
phenylindolo[2,1-a]isoquinolin-6-yl)propan-2-ols 6a−6m and
subsequent 5-phenyl-6-(prop-1-en-2-yl)indolo[2,1-a]-
isoquinolines products, 7a−7m, were obtained in moderate
to very good yields and in a highly regioselective manner. The
oxidative annulation can be scaled up to the 4 mmol scale with
the optimal reaction conditions, and 6j was isolated in 51%
yield (835 mg). It is worth noting that the Cl, Br, CN, NO
2
, or
CO
2
Me group remained intact after the oxidative annulation/
dehydration cascade process, showing an excellent functional
group tolerance.
Based on the above results and previous literature
studies,
11,12
a plausible mechanism of the coupling of 2-
phenyl-1H-indoles with propargylic alcohol derivatives is

subsequent C−H bond cleavage by the Cp*Rh(III) catalyst
gives five-membered rhoda(III)cycle II. Then, the migratory
insertion of propargylic alcohol derivatives into the Rh−C
bond in a regioselective manner via the weak coordination
between the rhodium atom and the oxygen atom provides a
seven-membered rhoda(III)cycle III. Intermediate III under-

In conclusion, we have successfully developed rhodium-
catalyzed NH-indole-directed C−H coupling with propargylic
alcohol derivatives for the diversity-oriented synthesis of
indole-fused polycyclic scaffolds. The reaction exhibits switch-
able regioselectivity depending on the propargylic alcohol
derivatives. With propargylic alcohol (free OH) as the coupling
partner, the reaction involves migratory insertion/reductive
elimination to generate 2-(5-phenylindolo[2,1-a]isoquinolin-6-
yl)propan-2-ols, which further undergo acid-mediated dehy-
dration to deliver 5-phenyl-6-(prop-1-en-2-yl)indolo[2,1-a]-
isoquinolines. Migratory insertion/β-OR elimination is in-
volved in the coupling reaction to afford ortho-allenylated-2-
phenyl-1H-indoles when the propargylic ester is used as the
coupling partner. Thereafter, taking advantage of the inherent
multiple reactivities of the allenyl motif, ortho-allenylated-2-
phenyl-1H-indoles can selectively convert into 5-phenyl-6-
(propan-2-ylidene)-5,6-dihydroindolo[2,1-a]isoquinolines via
base-mediated 6-endo-dig cyclization. On the other hand, 6-
(2-methylprop-1-en-1-yl)-6-phenyl-6H-isoindolo[2,1-a]indoles
could be obtained by palladium-catalyzed 5-exo-trig cyclization.
